Troubleshooting: typed errors, missing values, and resource limits

Source: vignettes/troubleshooting.Rmd
troubleshooting.Rmd

readboj fails closed through documented validation, transport, parser, cache, and resource checks when an input or source is not trustworthy. These expected failures retain a specific readboj_*_error class, so a pipeline can handle them without matching a fragile message string. An unexpected base or dependency error can still surface from manually malformed cache metadata or a third-party file; preserve the input identity and report that case.

All default examples here are local and deterministic. The package fixtures are synthetic and are labelled as such; they do not stand in for official BOJ values.

Identify a typed condition

An empty offline cache is a useful way to test a network policy without contacting the BOJ service. The failure is explicit and machine-readable:

offline_failure <- capture_error(read_boj_series(
  db = "FM08",
  code = "SYNTHM01",
  cache_dir = tempfile("readboj-empty-cache-"),
  offline = TRUE,
  wait = 0
))
offline_failure$class[1L]
#> [1] "readboj_offline_error"
offline_failure$message
#> [1] "No valid offline snapshot exists for https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/api/v1/getDataCode?code=SYNTHM01&db=FM08&format=json&lang=en."

The usual response is to check the cache path, the canonical query, and the max_age setting. If a connected refresh is permitted, rerun with refresh = TRUE; otherwise keep the call offline and report that the required snapshot is absent.

Input errors are separate from source availability. For example, duplicate series codes and reversed period bounds are rejected before any network request:

duplicate_codes <- capture_error(read_boj_series(
  db = "FM08", code = c("SYNTHM01", "SYNTHM01"),
  cache_dir = tempfile("readboj-no-request-"), offline = TRUE, wait = 0
))
reversed_period <- capture_error(read_boj_series(
  db = "FM08", code = "SYNTHM01",
  start_date = "202603", end_date = "202601",
  cache_dir = tempfile("readboj-no-request-"), offline = TRUE, wait = 0
))
c(duplicate = duplicate_codes$class[1L], reversed = reversed_period$class[1L])
#>                 duplicate                  reversed 
#> "readboj_parameter_error" "readboj_parameter_error"

Handle these as configuration or user-input issues. Do not retry a readboj_parameter_error as if it were a transient transport problem.

Distinguish size and schema failures

Every parser accepts a bound. A deliberately tiny byte bound raises a size condition before parsing starts:

size_failure <- capture_error(read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-page-1.json"),
  type = "data_json",
  db = "FM08",
  max_bytes = 10L
))
size_failure$class[1L]
#> [1] "readboj_size_error"
size_failure$message
#> [1] "Snapshot exceeds `max_bytes`."

The same principle applies to API cells/pages/codes, metadata rows, bulk ZIP entries and bytes, and workbook sheets/rows/columns/cells. Increase a bound only when the job’s memory and time budget supports it. API and archive readers do not silently return a partial table after crossing a declared limit.

Malformed or changed BOJ response fields raise readboj_schema_error; HTTP/API failures use more specific classes such as readboj_transport_error, readboj_auth_error, or readboj_api_error. Successful response bodies are cached only after transport and size checks pass, so a failed response should not become a valid offline object.

Preserve missing-value markers

Missing values have different representations in different official formats. The synthetic JSON fixture contains null, while the CSV fixture contains an empty field:

json <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-page-1.json"), type = "data_json", db = "FM08"
)
csv <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-en-page-1.csv"),
  type = "data_csv", db = "FM08", language = "en"
)

json[is.na(json$value), c("period", "value", "raw_value", "value_status")]
#>   period value raw_value value_status
#> 2 202602    NA      <NA>         null
csv[!nzchar(csv$raw_value), c("period", "value", "raw_value", "value_status")]
#>   period value raw_value value_status
#> 2 202602    NA                  blank

JSON missing values are labelled "null"; blank CSV cells are labelled "blank". read_boj_bulk() additionally retains source strings such as "NA" and "ND" in its value column and reports their marker in value_status. Treat these statuses as source semantics rather than replacing all missing-looking values with zero.

Encoding, credentials, and network checks

Japanese metadata and CSV responses use CP932 in the official interface. Pass the encoding explicitly when parsing a local response, and inspect both bilingual fields:

japanese <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("metadata-bilingual-cp932.csv"),
  type = "metadata_csv",
  db = "FM08",
  encoding = "CP932"
)
japanese[japanese$is_series, c("series_code", "name_en", "name_jp")]
#>   series_code                 name_en      name_jp
#> 2    SYNTHM01 Synthetic monthly index 合成月次指数
#> 3    SYNTHM02  Synthetic monthly rate 合成月次金利

The BOJ API is public: readboj has no credential argument and does not write secrets to URLs, cache indexes, or provenance. Requests use HTTPS and official BOJ hosts only. If an explicitly opted-in live call fails, first inspect the condition class, then distinguish a temporary network/rate-limit condition from an API error, authorization rejection, schema change, or local resource limit. Keep offline = TRUE in automated builds and use separately cached runs with READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true for live refreshes.

For the prescribed credit string, API notice, copyright link, and service release contact, inspect boj_api_credit() rather than copying a stale string into a report:

credit <- boj_api_credit()
credit[c("credit", "api_notice", "copyright", "service_release_contact")]
#> $credit
#> [1] "This service uses the API provided by the \"Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search.\" The Bank of Japan does not guarantee the content of the service."
#> 
#> $api_notice
#> [1] "https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/info/api_notice_en.pdf"
#> 
#> $copyright
#> [1] "https://www.boj.or.jp/en/about/copyright.htm"
#> 
#> $service_release_contact
#> [1] "post.rsd17@boj.or.jp"
